paper: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
authors: Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi, Shailesh Mishra, Christoph Endres, Thorsten Holz, Mario Fritz
venue: AISec 2023 (ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security)
threat_model: Indirect prompt injection via data that an application retrieves
detection_or_sanitization: None; case studies on real applications and GPT-4 synthetic apps
models_and_datasets: Bing Chat, code completion, GPT-4 applications
limitations: Does not evaluate a detector or a sanitizer
what_securerag_adds: Uses the threat this paper studies. SecureRAG adds a measured filter pipeline, not a new attack.
directly_comparable: Related threat; not a defense comparison

paper: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
authors: Yupei Liu, Yuqi Jia, Runpeng Geng, Jinyuan Jia, Neil Zhenqiang Gong
threat_model: Formal prompt-injection framework covering known attacks as special cases
defense_architecture: Benchmark of 5 attacks and 10 defenses on LLM-integrated tasks
detection_or_sanitization: Existing prevention and detection defenses, not sentence-window RAG sanitization
metrics: Attack success under a common framework
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG is narrower: one local 8B RAG stack and a 160-item private suite. It does not subsume this benchmark.
directly_comparable: Same problem family; different benchmark, so numbers are not comparable

paper: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
authors: Jingwei Yi, Yueqi Xie, Bin Zhu, Emre Kiciman, Guangzhong Sun, Xing Xie, Fangzhao Wu
threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in external content (BIPIA)
defense_architecture: Black-box boundary awareness and explicit reminder; white-box training defense
detection_or_sanitization: Prompt delimiters and reminders; not classifier-based sentence deletion
limitations: Defense is prompt or training based
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG filters text before generation instead of reformatting the prompt. It was not run on BIPIA.
directly_comparable: Same threat; different defense and dataset

paper: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
authors: Keegan Hines, Gary Lopez, Matthew Hall, Federico Zarfati, Yonatan Zunger, Emre Kiciman
venue: arXiv:2403.14720; a matching text is also in CEUR-WS Vol. 3920
peer_review_status: Preprint (CEUR copy not treated here as a separately verified journal article)
threat_model: Indirect prompt injection in untrusted data concatenated with user commands
limitations: Does not remove sentences; marks provenance
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG deletes flagged windows rather than marking them. No head-to-head evaluation exists.

paper: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
authors: Sizhe Chen, Julien Piet, Chawin Sitawarin, David Wagner
threat_model: Direct instructions hidden in the data channel
defense_architecture: Structured queries plus structured instruction tuning
detection_or_sanitization: Front-end formatting and a model trained to ignore data-channel instructions
models_and_datasets: Fine-tuned LLMs; manual and optimization attacks
limitations: Requires model training; not a plug-in filter for an unmodified generator
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG leaves Llama 3 weights unchanged and filters with rules and TF-IDF. It does not implement structured queries.

paper: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Wei Zou, Runpeng Geng, Binghui Wang, Jinyuan Jia
threat_model: A few optimized malicious texts inserted into a knowledge base and retrieved for a target question
defense_architecture: Attack paper; tested defenses were insufficient
models_and_datasets: RAG systems including large knowledge bases
limitations: Optimizes for retrieval, which the SecureRAG indirect suite does not
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG's indirect attacks are forced into the prompt. They do not answer whether a poisoned corpus would be retrieved.
directly_comparable: Not comparable until a retrieval-poisoning experiment is run

paper: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption (RobustRAG)
authors: Chong Xiang, Tong Wu, Zexuan Zhong, David Wagner, Danqi Chen, Prateek Mittal
peer_review_status: Peer-reviewed conference (accepted-paper listing on satml.org; proceedings pagination not verified here)
threat_model: Bounded number of malicious passages in the retrieved set
detection_or_sanitization: Keyword and decoding aggregation across isolated passages
models_and_datasets: Open-domain QA and long-form generation; multiple LLMs
metrics: Certified response quality and empirical robustness
limitations: Multiple LLM calls per query; different objective from keyword attack success
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG makes one generation call after filtering. It provides no certificate.

paper: Can Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks Be Detected and Removed?
authors: Yulin Chen, Haoran Li, Yuan Sui, Yufei He, Yue Liu, Yangqiu Song, Bryan Hooi
detection_or_sanitization: Trained detectors; segmentation removal and extraction removal
models_and_datasets: Crafted benchmark; existing and trained detectors
metrics: Detection accuracy and whether the injected instruction is removed
limitations: Removal quality depends on the detector; over-defense reported out of domain
what_securerag_adds: This is the closest peer-reviewed removal method. SecureRAG's window deletion is a simpler rule/TF-IDF instance of segmentation, evaluated on a different suite, with an explicit whole-chunk versus window utility split.
directly_comparable: Closest published removal baseline; datasets differ, so ASR cannot be compared

paper: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection (InstructDetector)
authors: Tongyu Wen, Chenglong Wang, Xiyuan Yang, Haoyu Tang, Yueqi Xie, Lingjuan Lyu, Zhicheng Dou, Fangzhao Wu
defense_architecture: White-box instruction detection from hidden states and gradients
models_and_datasets: In-domain and out-of-domain detection; BIPIA ASR
metrics: Detection accuracy; ASR reduced to 0.03% on BIPIA in the authors' report
limitations: Needs model internals. SecureRAG's generator is treated as a black box.
what_securerag_adds: Different detector; SecureRAG does not use hidden states

paper: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in RAG
authors: Huichi Zhou, Kin-Hei Lee, Zhonghao Zhan, Yue Chen, Zhenhao Li, Zhaoyang Wang, Hamed Haddadi, Emine Yilmaz
threat_model: Corpus poisoning of a RAG index
defense_architecture: Cluster filtering plus conflict self-assessment before generation
detection_or_sanitization: K-means on embeddings, cosine and ROUGE cues, LLM self-assessment
models_and_datasets: Multiple models and poisoning datasets in the preprint
metrics: Retrieval accuracy and attack resistance as reported by the authors
limitations: Preprint; clustering assumes poisoned documents form a separable group
what_securerag_adds: SecureRAG does not cluster the retrieved set. Its poisoned indexes were not used in the evaluated runs.
directly_comparable: Related only after a poisoning experiment

paper: A Sentence Relation-Based Approach to Sanitizing Malicious Instructions (SONAR)
authors: Soumil Datta, Melissa Umble, Daniel S. Brown, Guanhong Tao
threat_model: Indirect injection in retrieved or tool text
defense_architecture: NLI sentence graph and connectivity pruning
detection_or_sanitization: DeBERTa-style NLI entailment and contradiction; no TF-IDF risk score
models_and_datasets: Several models and datasets in the preprint
metrics: Attack success and clean-input fidelity, as reported by the authors
limitations: Preprint; uses a different signal than lexical rules
what_securerag_adds: SONAR already performs sentence-level sanitization with a stronger semantic signal. SecureRAG does not add NLI graph pruning. Its distinct measured result is the utility difference between whole-chunk deletion and window deletion on one private benchmark.
directly_comparable: Closest method family; not a result we can claim to exceed
